read_scope.notes: Read all 22 pages, including the abstract, main text, references, and Appendices A–G, from the frozen PDF. Visually inspected every rendered page, including Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–10; inspected the page 9 subsection heading at higher resolution to resolve a rendering-scale ambiguity. Consulted only the frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex for wording and locations. Verified the PDF SHA256 independently. The abstract contains 154 whitespace-delimited words in the PDF extraction. Technical appendices were treated as optional depth when judging main-text accessibility. Extraction and rendering used the isolated /tmp/editorial_r10_b_review directory. No other reviews, previous manuscripts, progress records, goals, or live manuscript files were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with manageable sentences and consistent explanations of alignment, total error, and reference contrasts. Section 4.1 gives both a measured lightness example and the no-response/exact/doubled-response comparison before the formal definitions. Qualifications generally explain a specific consequence rather than merely hedge. The broad ranking wording at the start of Section 5.5 and the compressed historical aside in Section 6 are localized refinements, not recurrent comprehension barriers.
score_reasons.structure: The progression from the name-versus-common-response question through the experimental arms, feature interpretation, contrast definitions, main results, pair diagnostics, calibration, and source correction is exceptionally coherent. Sections 4.4 and 5.3–5.5 make retrospective status visible, and Table 4 prevents the original source-sensitive comparison from being left as the final finding. Detailed estimators, simulations, provenance, and earlier cohorts stay in optional appendices. Only the brief historical-map aside in the Discussion interrupts this otherwise self-contained progression.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract identifies the experimental size, reference target, centering operation, principal results, and perceptual limit within 154 words. Sections 3.2–3.3 and Table 1 explain the arms and feature families; Section 4.1 makes beta and D interpretable before notation. Figures 1–3 and Tables 2–4 support reading the results without the repository. The distinction between fixed-scene uncertainty and unseen-scene generalization, and between calibrated vectors and changed images, is explicit. A small scope clarification in Section 5.5 would prevent a momentary apparent contradiction with the immediately preceding scene-averaging result.
score_reasons.engagement: The Monet–Sisley example gives the problem a concrete purpose, and the all-arm image grid, labeled contrast geometry, and pair heatmaps reward inspection. The narrative develops useful surprises: positive alignment without established improvement over no distinction, uneven pair coverage, and changes in ranking after calibration or scene averaging. Dense abstract calibration detail and an unexplained historical-map aside slightly reduce pace. The manuscript sustains interest through measured distinctions without claiming perceptual validation.

strengths: Section 4.1, page 5, connects an actual Monet–Sisley lightness gap (.325 in references versus .254 for GPT Image 2) to centering, then explains the D=1, 0, 1 outcomes for no, exact, and doubled contrasts. This makes the central method unusually accessible.

Figure 1, page 4, shows all six prompt conditions for every model with legible labeling and an explicit separation between generated controls and unmatched historical references. Its caption gives a useful viewing sequence and selection rule.

Figure 2, page 7, combines common overview axes with magnified Monet/Sisley/Pissarro details, while Figure 3, page 8, quantifies every painter pair. The visuals substantiate the move from aggregate alignment to uneven artist distinctions.

Section 5.4 and Table 3, page 9, explain why shrinking an already near-unit aligned response can reduce total error, and why averaging scenes can reverse the Nano Banana 2–FLUX ordering. Both numerical results receive concrete interpretation.
Section 5.5 and Table 4, pages 9–10, retain the source-correction changes to adjusted intervals and explicitly identify their retrospective status. The conclusion preserves that qualification.
The paper clearly separates numerical replay from exact-pixel re-extraction, AI source judgments from verified ground truth, and digital reference agreement from perceived artistic fidelity.

findings.issue: The opening statement that FLUX retains the lowest error point estimate across the reported scene sensitivities does not explicitly identify the uncalibrated, scene-by-scene score. Immediately above, Section 5.4 has shown a scene-averaged ordering in which Nano Banana 2 is lower than FLUX.
findings.reader_effect: A new reader can briefly interpret this as a contradiction or as a broader invariance of model ranking than the paper intends. The later text and tables allow the intended scope to be recovered.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the opening with: “For the uncalibrated scene-by-scene score, FLUX retains the lowest point estimate across scene deletions, measurement windows, reference targets and feature-weighting sensitivities (Appendices B–C).” This specifies the score and the scene operation without adding evidence or length.

findings.issue: The sentence about earlier feature maps showing opposing scaling effects introduces an unfamiliar historical analysis in compressed form. Neither the maps nor the relevant cohorts have been explained in the main text.
findings.reader_effect: The Discussion briefly stops developing the present result and requires an appendix detour to understand why this historical sentence belongs. The preceding statement about unidentified internal causes already communicates the main-text point.
findings.suggested_change: Cut this final historical-map sentence from the main Discussion and retain its complete evidence in Appendix F. Alternatively, replace it with a plain-language sentence about what the earlier result limits, funded by cutting the existing sentence. No new experiment or manuscript expansion is needed.

findings.issue: The calibration sentence combines the fitted parameter, the full 13-plus-1 rotation procedure, the ranking change, and the unchanged-image qualification. At this position the procedural clause takes attention away from the final substantive finding.
findings.reader_effect: The abstract remains understandable and within the word limit, but its final result requires more parsing than the earlier findings.
findings.suggested_change: Replace that sentence with: “One multiplier per model, fitted and evaluated on separate scenes, shifts the lowest estimated contrast error from FLUX.2 Max to GPT Image 2 without altering images.” Keep the exact rotating 13/1 procedure in Section 4.4. This shortens the abstract while preserving its evidence and claim boundaries.

summary: Excellent editorial communication of a deliberately bounded digital-reference comparison. The main narrative and findings are readily understood, the figures and tables are legible and useful, and the distinction between declared results, retrospective diagnostics, and perceptual claims is maintained. Remaining improvements are localized wording and pacing refinements that can be made by substitution or cuts within the existing 22-page and 155-word limits.
